processing: Made as Japanese green tea; Shizuoka research has also tested it as pan-fired kamairicha with good results.
harvest_season: Spring first flush, as is typical of Shizuoka green teas; its exact timing is rarely stated.
appearance_dry: As with other sencha, dark-green needles.
appearance_liquor: Clear pale yellow-green, typical of Shizuoka green tea.
appearance_wet: Soft green leaf, as is usual for steamed green tea.
taste_profile: A clean, refreshing aroma, with a first-flush flavour that rated well in a pan-fired trial.

brewing.notes: Normal sencha settings. For a pan-fired version, go up to about 80°C.

vintage_note: As with other Japanese green teas, it is sold as the current year's spring harvest and best drunk within a year. It turns up as small single-cultivar lots from Shizuoka growers rather than as a mainstream product.
description:
Okuhikari is a Japanese green tea cultivar connected with Shizuoka, where most of what is known about it comes from prefectural trials. Its aroma is the thing to notice: clean and refreshing, not sweet and lingering.

The usual processing for Japanese green tea applies, steaming first and then rolling and drying. It has also done well pan-fired: in a Shizuoka study of kamairicha, its first-flush flavour was among those rated highest.

Little is written about how it develops across steeps, so start it as you would any sencha, with cool water and about a minute, and adjust from there.

If you find a single-cultivar lot, try it alongside Shizukaori, its Shizuoka offspring, to see what the cross changed.
history: Little is documented about when or by whom Okuhikari was bred. It appears in Shizuoka research as a pan-fired candidate and as the seed parent of the early cultivar Shizukaori, from a 1989 cross with Kuritawase, so it was already in use by then.
